newsitem.title: CHINA: China says progress made in India border talks.
newsitem.headline: China says progress made in India border talks.

text.p: China said on Friday it had made progress in talks with India on the sensitive Himalayan border between the two Asian giants, with both sides agreeing to boost cross-border contacts.
A two-day meeting in Beijing between Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Tang Jiaxuan and Indian foreign secretary Salman Haider had ended with the agreement, Chinese state radio said.
Beijing and Delhi fought a brief war over sections of the 4,000-km (2,500-mile) border in 1962, but tensions have eased after years of talks.
The Beijing negotiations had resulted in progress on clarification of the Line of Actual Control between the two countries, state radio said but gave no details.
Both sides agreed to widen military training exchanges and to step up medium to high-level contacts. In one section of the disputed border two meeting points would be created, it said.
Talks on the border Line of Actual Control would continue, it said, but gave no timetable.
China and India agreed last year to pull back their troops from four military posts along the Himalayan border and to regulate potentially dangerous activity in the area.
The two countries agreed to work for peace and tranquillity along the frontier when then Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao visited Beijing in September 1993.
